About us

Global vision.
Local action.

Art of Living and the International Association for Human Values connect personal wellbeing, human values and service—then country teams turn that vision into practical work.

Our mission

Our mission is to transform lives by promoting positive values and proven techniques that foster wellbeing, resilience, and a stress-free, violence-free society.

Two organisations · one human purpose

Inner wellbeing meets sustainable service.

The organisations are connected by Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar’s vision, while each has its own role, governance and areas of work.

Art of Living

Strengthening the individual

Founded in 1981 by Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar, Art of Living is a global non-profit educational and humanitarian organisation. Its official global site reports active programmes in 182 countries, using breathwork, meditation, yoga and practical wisdom to support wellbeing and service.

Open the official global About page ↗
International Association for Human Values

Human values in sustainable development

IAHV uses a human-values-based approach to sustainable development, working through volunteers, trainers, innovators and community initiatives. Its stated mission centres on skilling and empowering individuals and communities through grassroots action.

Open the official IAHV profile ↗
Art of Living Africa

A continental public record

This website brings country programmes, approved media, local partnerships and verified impact records into one Africa-wide system—without erasing the local context behind the work.

Explore impact by country ↗

Founder and global peace ambassador

Peace begins within—and must move outward.

Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar founded Art of Living and the International Association for Human Values. His work connects personal transformation with humanitarian service, dialogue and a vision of a stress-free, violence-free society.

Across Africa, that vision is expressed through youth leadership, breath-based wellbeing, rehabilitation, education, culture, peace-building and community service.

Visit Gurudev’s official website ↗

The vision

“Unless we have a stress-free mind and a violence-free society, we cannot achieve world peace.”

Art of Living describes itself as a movement that strengthens the individual while bringing people of different cultures, traditions, religions and nationalities together.

IAHV extends that principle into human-values-based humanitarian and sustainable-development initiatives. The Africa network turns both into locally led programmes and service.

Home/Start with your breath.

Breath & mental wellbeing

Start with
your breath.

Breath awareness is simple, portable and immediate. It can create a pause — a place to meet the next moment with more clarity.

A one-minute reset

Let the exhale be a little longer.

Follow the circle. Breathe comfortably; there is nothing to force.

Ready?60seconds

Pause if you feel light-headed. This is a simple awareness exercise, not medical treatment.

60 seconds

  • Inhale gently for four
  • Pause softly for two
  • Exhale comfortably for six
  • Repeat without strain

Why breath is the thread

A practical bridge between inner experience and outward action.

01

Notice

Breath gives attention something immediate and physical to return to.

02

Regulate

A slower, more comfortable rhythm can help create a feeling of steadiness.

03

Respond

A pause can make space for a more deliberate next action.

Common questions

Keep it simple.

Do I need experience?

No. Start gently and stop if you feel uncomfortable.

Is this medical treatment?

No. This short guide is educational and does not replace professional medical or mental-health care.

Can a group learn together?

Yes. Use the Get Involved page to ask about an introductory session or a programme for your community.

Children & youth

Different ages.
Distinct pathways.

Children and young people need programmes designed for their stage of life. This is a separate programme family — not a label placed over every youth-facing project.

Country media profile

Botswana

Community wellbeing and dignity-focused activity at Sedibeng Foundation in Kopong Village.

Reporting scope

Two stakeholder submissions and eleven labelled photographs supplied in September 2026. Neither submission gives a calendar date; aggregate reach and consent records remain incomplete.

Kopong Village

Wellbeing alongside practical dignity support.

One submission describes the start of BWS with a 60-person group of older community members and support workers at Sedibeng Foundation, approximately 40 kilometres from Gaborone. Because the record does not separate participants from support staff, the figure is not added to the Africa-wide BWS total.

From Gaborone

Activity records

Submitted media

Movement, community and material support.

130 students build practical life skills.

Home/Impact/Breath Water Sound

Community wellbeing

Breath Water Sound

An experiential workshop helping children and young people navigate emotions, build resilience, express themselves and connect with others.

Source scope

Current country records supplied for Kenya, South Africa, Uganda, Nigeria and Ghana. Kenya reports 300+ participants; South Africa reports 13,670 participants since 2006; Uganda reports 400 students at City High School, Kampala; Nigeria reports 250 students at Command Day Army School plus 300 participants at St Monica Catholic Church in 2018; and Ghana reports 130 students at Kpone Presbyterian JHS in March 2026. Figures are programme-specific and may not represent unique people.

Life skills through breath, water and sound.

What this work is designed to change.

15,050+participants across current Kenya, South Africa, Uganda, Nigeria and Ghana Breath Water Sound records

Focus areas

  • Breath
  • Emotional intelligence
  • Confidence
  • Life skills
  • Connection
  • Resilience
  • Human values

What participants build

01

Breath

Simple techniques offer a practical way to settle, focus and meet difficult emotions.

02

Water

Guided reflection uses adaptability and letting go as an accessible life-skills metaphor.

03

Sound

Music, rhythm and voice create room for expression, play and connection.

From practice to participation

Change has to travel beyond the room.

  1. 01

    Meet the group

    Facilitators create a safe, participatory environment rather than a lecture.

  2. 02

    Experience the tools

    Young people learn by breathing, moving, listening, reflecting and creating together.

  3. 03

    Carry it forward

Pause together

Belong to a continent

The campaign frames peace as a Pan-African intention carried by people across countries and communities.

Rehabilitation

Prison SMART

A two-stage rehabilitation pathway supporting people in correctional facilities with breath-based tools for stress, emotional resilience, responsibility and positive relationships.

Source scope

Stakeholder-approved country records for South Africa, Kenya and Uganda; client-supplied photography and anonymous testimonials; and the public January 2023 Kwale GoK Prison programme post. South Africa source documents conflict at 12,319 versus 12,505+, so this site uses the defensible rounded figure 12,300+ pending reconciliation.

Stress management, rehabilitation and deeper reflection behind bars.

What this work is designed to change.

15,300+participants across current South Africa, Kenya and Uganda records

Focus areas

  • Stress management
  • Breath-based practices
  • Meditation
  • Trauma and emotional resilience
  • Human values
  • Rehabilitation
  • Reflection and silence

What participants build

01

A pause before reaction

Breath awareness can create space between a difficult feeling and the response that follows.

02

Emotional resilience

Participants build practical habits for meeting stress, frustration and isolation.

03

Reconnection

Human values and responsibility support healthier relationships with self and others.

The two-stage pathway

Foundation first. Deeper reflection follows.

  1. 01

    Prison SMART

    The foundational programme introduces stress-management skills, breathwork, meditation, human values and practical tools for handling difficult emotions.

  2. 02

    Prepare and practise

    Feeder programmes and continued practice prepare eligible participants for a deeper experience of meditation and reflection.

  3. 03

    Art of Silence

    A four-day advanced programme gives qualifying participants a sustained period of silence, meditation and guided reflection.

Regional reach

Documented in South Africa, Kenya and Uganda.

Current figures are taken from stakeholder-approved country records. South Africa’s two supplied totals differ, so 12,300+ is used until the exact figure is reconciled.

Krugersdorp · Gauteng · 14–17 October 2025

Four days of silence after months of preparation.

Krugersdorp Correctional Centre hosted a four-day Art of Silence advanced meditation programme for 40 participants — the first silence course reported there in 15 years.

The experience followed a two-to-three-month preparation journey, including two feeder Prison SMART programmes that helped participants build the foundation for deeper silence and reflection.

Documentary · A film by Irina Semenova

When Dreams Learn to Breathe

Stories Of Transformation

In the heart of Kenya’s largest slums, hope and transformation are blossoming through the efforts of The Art of Living Foundation. The youth, once caught in cycles of hardship and limited opportunities, are now discovering a path to personal growth and empowerment.

Through specialized Art of Living programs, these young minds are learning to overcome emotional challenges, build confidence, and unlock their potential. The teachers of Art of Living are working tirelessly to uplift these communities by offering tools for stress relief, mental well-being, and personal development.

Meditation, breathwork, and life skills training have become the cornerstones of these young individuals’ journeys toward a brighter future.
